newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, with Wall St jitters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, with Wall St jitters.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Thursday with investors jittery over how Wall Street would open after its overnight fall further undermined New York's recent record-breaking run.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened slightly but traders anxiously awaited U.S. consumer price figures due at 1330 GMT for clues on the health of the American economy.

London, Europe's biggest stock market, made the heftiest gains, climbing 0.5 percent although business was light and investors edgy because of the Dow Jones industrials' one percent drop on Wednesday.

Stocks and bonds in New York had tumbled on renewed fears of an interest rate hike and fresh worries about corporate earnings. The Dow had in fact fallen by two percent before recovering some poise at the close.

London's performance hid a fragile mood. Investors were nervous that another dip in Wall Street later in the day could be be a fatal blow for New York's bull run, already hit by the U.S. Federal Reserve's warning about "irrational exuberance" in the markets.

Others were more optimistic. "It is looking now like Wall Street will have a stronger start today which has helped us regain some ground," the head of sales and trading at a major investment bank said.
"We'll just drift around until we see how the Dow opens," another trader said. "I don't really expect any serious buying or selling until we see whether or not the Dow can spring back."
In Frankfurt, which ended sharply down on Wednesday, stocks slipped in an out of the plus column but were down by mid-morning as profit-taking eroded early gains.'
Floor trading had edged up in early transaction as the steady dollar helped dispel worries over New York's weak close.

The stronger dollar helped boost some chemical sector shares because of enhanced export prospects, with Hoechst attracting interest after announcing that it would sell off its specialty chemicals business to Swiss group Clariant.
In Paris, stocks slipped a few points in early trade then clawed back the losses to squeeze into positive territory. "The market is fragile," a trader said.

On the currency front, the dollar found a firm foothold above 1.54 marks and 113 yen as stock and bond markets recovered some poise and as European Union leaders moved closer to agreement on a budgetary stability pact this weekend.
The dollar's role as a safe haven currency would be enhanced once the mark is merged into the proposed single European currency and agreement on the stability pact is seen as paving the way.
"The comments we've been seeing throughout the morning make it more likely that we will see agreement on a stability pact at the weekend," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.22 yen and 1.5453 marks against 112.92 and 1.5412 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 17.3 points higher at 3,999.8
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 1.44 points at 2,214.72.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt slipped 1.09 points to to 2,839.96.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $368.60 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $368.65. Silver was unchanged at $4.83.
